glosses: To succeed in something, now especially in academic performance.
To carry out successfully; to accomplish.

examples.text: achieve goals
achieve objectives
You can achieve anything if you put your mind to it.
Hannah achieved her lifelong dream of winning a medal at the Olympics.
Supposing faculties and powers to be the same, far more may be achieved in any line by the aid of a capital, invigorating motive than without it.

glosses: To conclude, finish, especially successfully.

examples.text:
Full many Countreyes they did overronne,
 From the uprising to the setting Sunne,
 And many hard adventures did atchieve […]

glosses: To obtain, or gain (a desired result, objective etc.), as the result of exertion; to succeed in gaining; to win.

examples.text: I was about to say that I had known the Celebrity from the time he wore kilts. But I see I will have to amend that, because he was not a celebrity then, nor, indeed, did he achieve fame until some time after I left New York for the West.

Some are born great, some achieve greatness.

glosses: To conclude, to turn out.

examples.text:

examples.text: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I can not attain unto it.

glosses: To obtain; to acquire.

examples.text: I'm going to get a computer tomorrow from the discount store.

glosses: To cause to come or go or move.

glosses: To adopt, assume, arrive at, or progress towards (a certain position, location, state).

examples.text: The actors are getting into position.

glosses: To cover (a certain distance) while travelling.

examples.text: to get a mile

glosses: (with full infinitive or gerund-participle) To begin (doing something or to do something).

examples.text: We ought to get moving or we'll be late.

glosses: To take or catch (a scheduled transportation service).

examples.text: I normally get the 7:45 train.

glosses: To respond to (a telephone call, a doorbell, etc).

examples.text: Can you get that call, please? I'm busy.

glosses: (with full infinitive) To be able, be permitted, or have the opportunity (to do something desirable or ironically implied to be desirable).

examples.text: I'm so jealous that you got to see them perform live!

examples.text: He got bitten by a dog.

glosses: Used with a pronoun subject, usually you but sometimes one, to indicate that the object of the verb exists, can occur or is otherwise typical.

examples.text: You get some very rude people here.

examples.text: Quand j'atteignais un rat d'un bon coup de fouet, le ronge-maille sifflait avec fureur, hérissait tous ses poils et s'élançait avec désespoir contre le fouet lui-même, instrument de sa torture; […].

glosses: Parvenir à un terme, à quelque chose dont on était plus ou moins éloigné, en parlant des choses aussi bien que des personnes.

examples.text: Nous atteignons bientôt la région des nuages, et la température tombe si bas, que le froid nous mord horriblement les mains et les pieds.

glosses: Parvenir à son but, en causant un dommage physique ou moral, en parlant de choses.
